description: Holds attendance log records (defined in the EF Core model), linked to users.
business_purpose: Used to track and report attendance log records for the HR & User Management area.
record_granularity: One row represents one attendance log.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Unique identifier of the attendance log.

columns.name: is_deleted
columns.description: Soft-delete flag. True when the record has been deleted.

columns.name: related_id
columns.description: Related id of the attendance log.

columns.name: related_section
columns.description: Related section of the attendance log.

columns.name: userId
columns.description: Reference to the users linked to this attendance log.

relationships.description: Each attendance log references one users (user).

business_rules: Deleted records (is_deleted = 1) should normally be excluded from reporting.
logdate is the preferred date column for period-based reporting.
Join to Users through the foreign key columns to resolve names.
AttendanceLog is defined in the EF Core model but was not found in the connected database, so it may not be deployed there.

query_notes: Do not generate SQL against AttendanceLog: no table or view with this name exists in the connected database.
Always filter is_deleted = 0 unless deleted records are explicitly requested.
Use COUNT(DISTINCT id) when counting attendance log records; joins can duplicate rows.
To resolve names, join on: userId = Users.Id.
Defined in the EF Core model but not found in the connected database; confirm it has been migrated before relying on it.
